(PER: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE P SREE SUDHA)
Though the appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
2. This appeal is filed against the judgment and award dated 22.08.2022 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal No.XV, Vijayapura, in MVC No.1372 of 2019.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal No.XV, Vijayapura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. The claimant aged 14 years, student met with an accident on 27.07.2019 due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing registration NC: 2025:KHC-K:6624 HC-KAR No.MH-11/BH-5934 and sustained grievous injures.
She was represented by her father as a natural guardian and filed a claim petition before the Tribunal, claiming compensation of Rs.38,00,000/-.

4. The Tribunal, considering the entire evidence on record, granted an amount of Rs.3,22,839 towards medical expenses and a global sum of Rs.25,000/- under all conventional heads and thereby granted a total compensation of Rs.3,48,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation and directed respondent No.2-Insurance Company to deposit the same.
5.

Aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the injured claimant has preferred this appeal, in which it is contended that, the appellant was earning Rs.10,000/- per month, but the Tribunal erred in not taking the income and not awarding any compensation towards loss of future earning; she sustained fracture and suffering from permanent physical impediment; she spent Rs.5,00,000/-

; the Tribunal has granted NC: 2025:KHC-K:6624 HC-KAR meagre amount under conventional heads.
Therefore, requested for enhancement of compensation.

6. Heard the arguments of both sides.
7.

As per the wound certificate - Ex.P7, the appellant has sustained right ear bleed sutured wound approximately infront of right ear, abrasion over left forearm, abrasion over right forearm, abrasion over dorsum of left foot, brain-TBI, left temporal contusion and right temporal EDH with DAI.
The nature of injuries is not mentioned in the said certificate.

But, in the discharge summary, it is mentioned that, she was admitted in the hospital on 27.07.2019 and discharged on 11.08.2019 and thus, she was hospitalised for 15 days and it was diagnosed as traumatic brain injury with diffuse axonal injury with left temporal haemorrhagic contusion with right parieto temporal SDH.
The appellant has not examined the doctor and as such, the disability was not assessed and thereby, the Tribunal has not awarded any amount towards loss of future earning.

However, considering the NC:
2025:KHC-K:6624 HC-KAR nature of injuries, period of hospitalisation and the age of the appellant, this Court finds it reasonable to take the disability at 10% as per the citation of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mallikarjun vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Company Limited and Another1 and thus, the appellant is entitled for Rs.1,00,000/- towards pain and suffering already undergone and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock, hardship,
inconvenience and discomfits, etc. and loss of amenities in life on account of permanent disability.
8.

sentences.text: The father of the appellant is doing agriculture and he was aged 45 years and the accident occurred in the year 2019.

Hence, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.10,000/-
for discomfort, inconvenience and loss of earnings to the parents during the period of hospitalisation.

The Tribunal has granted an amount of Rs.3,22,839/- towards medical expenses and Rs.25,000/-
towards conventional heads, in all Rs.3,48,000/-, which is just and proper and needs no interference.

10. Hence, the appellant is entitled for the modified compensation under different heads as below:

The Insurance Company has already deposited the amount awarded by the Tribunal.
Thus, the appellant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.1,10,000/- with NC: 2025:KHC-K:6624 HC-KAR interest at 6% per annum and therefore, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

11. In the result, the following order is passed:
 (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The appellant/claimant is entitled for the enhanced compensation of Rs.1,10,000/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
(iii) Respondent No.2-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount within one month from the date of this judgment.
(iv) On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
